CIV.note: Nothing stated about the central bank.
Nothing stated about civil servant training.
Online fraud and abuse prevalence is stated, but no financial consumer rule or complaints body.
Transfers abroad appear only as a share of mobile money transaction types, with no named corridor.
Rural and urban splits are for household internet access, not for people using the internet; no rural connection programme is stated.
Digital skills are mentioned only as a general gap; no programme or measured share.
Nothing stated about government payments to people.

facts.fact: ARTCI's national MSI 2024 household survey puts internet use at 41.4% of individuals aged 5 and over (11,276,214 people), men 44.5% and women 38.3%.
ARTCI's MSI 2024 survey finds 50.3% of individuals aged 5 and over hold a personal mobile money account, over 13 million people (men 55.4%, women 45.1%); the base is not adults.
ARTCI's MSI 2024 survey reports 13,695,257 people (50.3% of those aged 5 and over) using mobile money, mainly for money transfers, airtime purchase and bill payment, with some merchant payments.

CIV.note: Administrative acts appear only as a small share of mobile money transactions; no tax or fee payment is stated.
Only a household electricity share (rural 92.9%) is given; the study's figure is the World Bank rural access series.
